Method of Attack: UEFI bootkit malware that evades antivirus detection, resists removal attempts, disables security features such as Defender, HVCI, BitLocker
Writes malicious bootloader files to EFI system partition and locks them to prevent deletion or modification
Disables Hypervisor-protected Code Integrity (HVCI) by modifying registry keys
Injects HTTP downloader function to connect to command and control (C2) server
Deploys payloads early in the boot process to disable security mechanisms
Impacted Systems: Windows operating system devices with UEFI firmware
Attack Vector: Requires privileged access (remote or physical) to install UEFI bootkit
Initial access via first-stage threat or initial access vector preceding UEFI malware deployment
Indicators of Compromise: Recently created and locked bootloader files in EFI system partition (ESP)
Presence of staging directory in EPS:/filesystem
Registry key modification for HVCI (Enabled value set to 0)
Network logs showing outbound connections from winlogon.exe on port 80
Windows Event Logs entries under Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational Log
Event ID 7023 in System event log (Defender service stopped unexpectedly)
Boot configuration logs (MeasuredBoot logs) showing added or removed boot drivers grubx64.efi and winload.efi
Presence of /system32/ directory on ESP after file deletion
File access errors when calculating hash of locked bootloader files
